kos.desc: Lets the assistant search and read the Gbrain cross-domain knowledge graph: semantic retrieval, keyword full-text, read a whole page, find domain experts, list pages by type/tag, and see what links to a page.
kos.control: Core read · always registered; retrieval depends on whether Gbrain is configured.

selfMount.desc: Lets the assistant view/update its own identity docs and discover/mount skills (update_system_md / discover_skills / set_skill_enabled).

session.title: Session retrieval
session.desc: Lets the assistant search your past AI conversation history (list / search / read).

Separate multiple Tavily keys with commas to auto-rotate when one runs out of quota; leave empty to use DuckDuckGo (unreachable in China). Stored only in the local .env, never returned to the UI. Takes effect on save.

standingDocs.floorNote: PRODUCT_SAFETY_FLOOR is always prepended at the code layer — document content cannot weaken it. Override phrasing in RULES is rejected server-side.
standingDocs.memoryNote: memory.md is auto-extracted and rewritten by the AI from your conversations, and you can also edit it manually. It is injected into every conversation as BACKGROUND memory (not an identity doc) and cannot weaken the safety floor.
standingDocs.overBudgetHint: Content exceeds the {budget}-character budget; trim it before saving.

execPolicy.title: Automation policy
execPolicy.helper: The assistant needs your approval every time it runs a command or reads/writes files. This is the allowlist you built via “Always allow” for exact operations: matching operations run without approval, everything else still prompts. To loosen a rule, delete and recreate it (in-place editing is not supported, to avoid silently widening scope).
execPolicy.empty: No automation policies yet. When the assistant asks to run a command or read/write files, tick “Always allow” to create an allowlist entry for that exact operation — matching operations then run without approval.

folderSizeLimit.label: IMAP folder view limit (messages)
folderSizeLimit.helper: Exposes only the most recent N messages of each folder over IMAP. On a large mailbox (over 10,000 messages) an unlimited view makes DavMail enumerate the whole folder over EWS on every sync — slow enough to time out and stall the entire sync chain. The cost: older messages outside the window are invisible at the IMAP layer (history already synced locally is unaffected; this only limits what incremental sync and write operations such as flag / archive can reach). Default 500; set 0 to leave this key entirely to DavMail.

status.updated: Written to the DavMail config file ({path} → davmail.folderSizeLimit={desired}). DavMail only reads its config at startup, so restart the DavMail bridge (pm2 restart davmail-poc) for it to take effect.
status.unchanged: The DavMail config file already has {value} ({path}); nothing to change.
status.fileMissing: DavMail config file not found, so this setting has no effect right now: {path}. Point DAVMAIL_ROOT in .env at your DavMail directory, or add davmail.folderSizeLimit={desired} to davmail.properties by hand.
status.error: Failed to write the DavMail config file, so this setting may have no effect: {path} (see the backend log for the reason).
status.disabled: Set to 0: MailAgent leaves this key alone and DavMail uses its own config value (currently {value}).
status.disabledUnset: Set to 0: MailAgent leaves this key alone, and the DavMail config file doesn't set it either (risky on large mailboxes).

policy.errOriginRequired: Enter the domain or full URL to allow.
policy.originPlaceholder: Domain or full URL, e.g. api.vendor.com or https://api.vendor.com
policy.originHint: An approval-free web domain (the gated-tier whitelist). On submit the server normalizes it to scheme://host:port and echoes it back; different case / port / subdomain count as different origins, and subdomains do not inherit.
policy.warnBody: Once created, "{agent}" will execute {action} without asking you. The rule only applies to {mode}; delete it to restore per-action approval.

grant.label: Allow running local skill scripts (grant_exec)
grant.hint: Opens the exec surface for this agent's unattended runs. Execution still requires a whitelist rule match plus a first-run approval on the Dynamic Island; without a match it pauses per action. Takes effect after saving.
grant.warn: High risk: once enabled, unattended runs of "{agent}" may request executing local skill scripts. Enable?

web.label: Web access (grant_web)
web.hint: Whether this agent's unattended runs may reach the web, and the approval-free scope. Takes effect after saving.
web.searchWarn: Both gated and open allow web_search without approval: the search query goes straight to DuckDuckGo, no per-call prompt.
web.openWarn: Fully open: this agent may fetch any URL without approval — smuggled data can be encoded into the URL and exfiltrated, with only SSRF protection as a backstop.
web.untrustedOpenWarn: Email trigger × fully-open web is the largest exposure combination: a poisoned email can steer content into outbound requests. Enable only for agents you trust.
web.gatedHint: Gated tier: web_fetch is approval-free only when the URL matches a domain in the whitelist below; other domains pause per call (with an "always allow this domain" affordance on the card).

mounts.label: Mounted skills
mounts.hint: The skills visible to this agent's unattended runs (a narrowing surface). Tools of unmounted skills are unavailable to this agent; mounting cannot revive a globally disabled skill.
mounts.empty: Explicit zero mount: this agent has no skill tools.
